mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2.5% annualized over the previous two months signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL annualized increase exceeds 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points over the previous month signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances where UNRATE decreases by more than 0.5pp.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over the previous two months signals increased demand for housing and related goods, which is a leading indicator of economic growth, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in > 50% of instances where HOUST increases.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 4%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS exceeds 4%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 over the previous month, combined with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.2 percentage points, signals a robust labor market, which boosts economic activity and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increase > 200k and UNRATE decrease > 0.2pp in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances where both conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over the previous two months signals a contraction in supply, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where INDPRO decreases by more than 1%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over the previous month signals increased consumer demand, which is a strong indicator of economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in > 50% of instances where RSAFS increases.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is increasing at an annualized rate of more than 3% over the previous two months, it signals an environment of easy monetary policy with inflationary pressure, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: inflationary pressure with accommodative monetary policy
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances where both conditions are met.
